title: Angular events under the planar Gaussian measure
statement: Let $s\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ and let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be measurable, with $A\subseteq(-\pi,\pi)$. Suppose that for every polar coordinate pair $p=(r,\theta)$ with $r>0$ and $-\pi<\theta<\pi$, the point with polar coordinates $(r,\theta)$ lies in $s$ exactly when $\theta\in A$. Then the product of two standard Gaussian measures assigns to $s$ the measure $\left(\int_0^\infty r\,\varphi(r)\varphi(0)\,dr\right)|A|$, where $\varphi$ is the standard Gaussian density and $|A|$ is the Lebesgue measure of $A$.
hypotheses_covered: For every polar coordinate pair in the polar-coordinate domain, membership of its corresponding point in $s$ is equivalent to its angle belonging to $A$
